## Example 4

Before we move ahead, let's consider one final example:

```text
T(n)=2T(n2)+Ө(n2log⁡2n)T\lparen n\rparen = 2T \left( \cfrac{n}{2} \right) + Ө\lparen n^2 \log ^2 n \rparenT(n)=2T(2n​)+Ө(n2log2n)
```

Let's calculate its time complexity using the master theorem.

Step 1: Compare the recurrence relation with the general form.

The general form of T(n) is:

```text
T(n)=aT(nb)+Ө(nk(log⁡n)p)T\lparen n\rparen = aT \left( \cfrac{n}{b} \right) + Ө\lparen n^k \lparen \log n \rparen ^p \rparenT(n)=aT(bn​)+Ө(nk(logn)p)
```

Step 2: Rewrite the recurrence relation to match the general form.

```text
T(n)=2T(n2)+Ө(n2(log⁡n)2)T\lparen n\rparen = 2T \left( \cfrac{n}{2} \right) + Ө\lparen n^2 \lparen \log n \rparen ^2 \rparenT(n)=2T(2n​)+Ө(n2(logn)2)
```

Step 3: Identify a, b, k, and p and check the conditions for the master theorem.

```python
a = 2
b = 2
k = 2
p = 2
```

Since a≥1a \geq 1a≥1, b > 1, k≥0k \geq 0k≥0, and p is a real number, the master theorem is possible.

Step 4: Compare log⁡ba\log_balogb​a and k and apply the matching rule.

Here,

```text
log⁡ba=log⁡22=1\log_ba = \log_22 = 1logb​a=log2​2=1k=2k = 2k=2
```

Since log⁡ba<k\log_ba < klogb​a<k and p≥0p \geq 0p≥0, let's apply the formula to find the time complexity for this scenario.

```text
T(n)=Ө(nk(log⁡n)p)T\lparen n\rparen = Ө(n^k (\log n)^p)T(n)=Ө(nk(logn)p)T(n)=Ө(n2(log⁡n)2)\hphantom{T\lparen n \rparen} = Ө(n^2 (\log n)^2)T(n)=Ө(n2(logn)2)T(n)=Ө(n2log⁡2n)\hphantom{T\lparen n \rparen} = Ө(n^2 \log ^2 n)T(n)=Ө(n2log2n)
```
